palette.notes: An index, not one artwork. The palette list holds thousands of palettes filterable by exact or max colour count and tags (hardware, artist, gameboy); popular ones range from 4 to 31 colours.

lighting: No dedicated lighting tutorial in the index; the closest entry is a shading tutorial by Pedro Medeiros.
silhouette: Not covered directly; the index points to beginner guides (e.g. Pixel Logic) that cover basic forms.

motion.timing: No timing of its own; links tutorials tagged animation and walkcycle (e.g. saint11 walk cycle, fabric/flags). No idle-specific tutorial listed.

texture: Tutorial tags include dithering, texture, grass, rocks, water, trees and tilesets, so texture is treated per material.
camera: No camera content; background and tileset tutorials are listed for scene building.

acting.acts: No characters shown; as a staging lesson it suggests treating character, background and material as separate, learnable pieces.

techniques: pick a fixed palette by exact colour count before drawing
filter palettes by tag (hardware look like gameboy vs artist-made)
learn materials one at a time (water, grass, fabric) from tagged tutorials
use Aseprite's outline feature for quick consistent outlines
feel: fixed small palette from a shared library + one tutorial per material = consistent look without reinventing
for_fred: Lock Fred, Pixie and every background to one Lospec palette of a fixed size (e.g. 16-32 colours) so props added later never clash. For new motion, look up the tagged material tutorial (water for Fred's tank, fabric for flags) instead of inventing a new loop.
